source.author: verg
source.text: Tu, dea, tu praesens nostro succurre labori, astrorum decus et nemorum Latonia custos Siqua tuis umquam pro me pater Hyrtacus aris dona tulit, siqua ipse meis venatibus auxi suspendive tholo aut sacra ad fastigia fixi:
source.text_original: 'Tu, dea, tu praesens nostro succurre labori, / astrorum decus et nemorum Latonia custos / Siqua tuis umquam pro me pater Hyrtacus aris / dona tulit, siqua ipse meis venatibus auxi / suspendive tholo aut sacra ad fastigia fixi: /
source.text_english: You, goddess, you, be present and aid our toil, glory of the stars and Latonia, guardian of the groves. If ever my father Hyrtacus brought any gifts for me to your altars, if ever I myself increased them with my hunts or hung them from the temple roof or fixed them to the sacred heights:

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: tu, cui iam curaeque vigent animique viriles, i, decus, et pecoris Nephelaei vellera Graio redde tholo ac tantis temet dignare periclis.
reuse.text_original: tu, cui iam curaeque vigent animique viriles, / i, decus, et pecoris Nephelaei vellera Graio / redde tholo ac tantis temet dignare periclis.
reuse.text_english: You, in whom now both cares and manly courage are strong, go, my glory, and restore to the Greek shrine the fleece of the Nephelaean flock, and deem yourself worthy of so great dangers.
